findings.span: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
findings.note: The question is left entirely in English, so a Czech player hearing it read aloud cannot understand or answer it in Czech — the item is unplayable.
The correct answer was changed from "Iron" (Železo) to "Olovo" (lead), so a Czech player who correctly says "železo" is graded wrong.

findings.span: Značka Fe pochází z latinského plumbum.
findings.note: The explanation replaces Latin "ferrum" with "plumbum", making it factually false and reinforcing the wrong answer instead of supporting iron.
The source unit "metres" was changed to "mil" (miles), so the stated answer is factually false and a Czech player answering "8 849 metrů" would be graded wrong.
The alternative answer likewise says miles instead of metres, and the second English alternative ("roughly 8.8 kilometres") was dropped, removing a valid spoken answer for the player.

findings.span: Vrchol se tyčí 8 849 mil nad mořskou hladinou.
findings.note: The explanation repeats the wrong unit, so it no longer supports the correct answer and misinforms the player.
The correct answer moved from a) Vltava to b) Labe, so the Czech item now grades the true answer (Vltava) as wrong and rewards a factually false one.

findings.span: Labe protéká Prahou a severněji se vlévá do Vltavy.
findings.note: The explanation reverses the source's rivers, asserting the false claim that the Elbe flows through Prague into the Vltava, reinforcing the flipped answer instead of supporting the correct one.
The option values are ordinary words left in English while the question asks "Pravda nebo nepravda", so a player answering aloud in Czech ("pravda") cannot match the offered options.
The correct answer is left in English, so a Czech player's spoken "pravda" will not be graded as matching the stored answer.
The Czech release title of 'The Godfather' is 'Kmotr'; 'Kmotřenec' means 'godson' and is an invented title, so a player who correctly says 'Kmotr' is graded wrong.

findings.span: Repluku pronáší Vito Corleone ve filmu Kmotřenec.
findings.note: The explanation repeats the wrong film title, so it no longer supports the real answer 'Kmotr' and reinforces the ungradable answer key.

The English sense of "rotate" (swap wheel positions) is carried into the Czech verb "rotovat", which means to spin/revolve; a native would say "prohazovat/přehazovat pneumatiky", so the heard question sounds like it asks how often tyres should spin.
Same calqued verb in the explanation; the noun "rotace pneumatik" is at least semi-established in Czech service jargon, so the harm here is only stylistic.

The German exonym Joachimsthal was replaced by the Czech name Jáchymov, which is the correct answer — the question now hands the player the answer outright and is also factually false (the German name is not "Jáchymov").

findings.span: Proč cibule dělají tebe plakat, když je sekáš?
findings.note: Word-for-word calque of the English causative "make you cry" with a wrongly placed stressed pronoun "tebe"; Czech would say e.g. "Proč z cibule slzí oči, když ji krájíš?" — understandable but clearly non-native.
Redundant English-style subject pronoun, and "oni" is the masculine animate form while the referent "cibule" is feminine ("ony" at most, normally omitted); a native would correct it.

Literal rendering of "causes irritation" with the verb "dělat"; Czech says "dráždí oči" or "způsobuje podráždění očí" — same wrong pattern also in the alternative answer "sirná sloučenina dělá podráždění očí".

findings.span: která dělá reakci s vlhkostí v oku
findings.note: Calque of "reacts with"; Czech requires "reaguje s vlhkostí v oku", so the explanation reads as non-Czech.
"sekat" is the wrong verb for chopping an onion in Czech (used for mowing/hacking); "krájet" is standard and is in fact used in the explanation, making the item internally inconsistent.
The song title, which is the correct answer, was literally translated instead of kept as "Bohemian Rhapsody"; a player who says the real title aloud will be graded wrong.

findings.span: a) Bohémská rapsodie | b) Rozhýbeme tě | c) Někoho k milování
findings.note: Queen song titles in the options were translated into invented Czech forms, so the spoken originals no longer match the option set and the distractors are unrecognisable.
